templates.pattern: [P1] starts from O, walks [D1] km North to A, then [D2] km East to B, then [D3] km South to C, then [D4] km West to D, then [D5] km North to E. What is the straight-line distance from O to E?
templates.explanation: Net North=[D1]-[D3]+[D5]. Net East=[D2]-[D4]. Distance=√(Net_N²+Net_E²)

templates.pattern: Four persons [P1],[P2],[P3],[P4] stand at four corners of a square with side [D1] km. [P1] is at NW, [P2] at NE, [P3] at SE, [P4] at SW. Each walks towards the centre. How far does each walk?
templates.explanation: Distance from corner to centre of square with side [D1] = ([D1]×√2)/2 = [D1]/√2

templates.pattern: [P1] goes [D1] km East, turns left, goes [D2] km, turns left, goes [D3] km, turns right, goes [D4] km, turns right, goes [D5] km. In which direction is [P1] from start?
templates.explanation: E[D1]→N[D2]→W[D3]→N[D4]→E[D5]. Net E=[D1-D3+D5], Net N=[D2+D4]. Both positive → North-East.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts from village A and walks [D1] km South to B, [D2] km West to C, [D3] km North to D, [D4] km East to E, [D5] km North to F. What is the direction of F from A and distance?
templates.explanation: Net N=[D3-D1+D5], Net E=[D4-D2]. If both positive → NE. Distance=√(Net_N²+Net_E²)

templates.pattern: In a town, roads run only North-South and East-West. [P1] is at intersection O. Post office is [D1] km North and [D2] km East. Bank is [D3] km South and [D4] km West of O. What is the road distance from post office to bank?
templates.explanation: Road distance (Manhattan) = (N-S distance) + (E-W distance) = ([D1]+[D3]) + ([D2]+[D4])

templates.pattern: [P1] starts from O. Goes [D1] km North. Turns 135 degrees clockwise. Walks [D2] km. Turns 135 degrees clockwise. Walks [D3] km. In which direction is [P1] from O?
templates.explanation: North + 135° CW = South-East. SE + 135° CW = North-East direction roughly. But D2=D3 and turns are symmetric. Net effect: moving North initially, then SE then back NE. Final direction from O is North.

templates.pattern: [P1],[P2],[P3] start from point O at the same time. [P1] goes [D1] km North. [P2] goes [D1] km East. [P3] goes [D1] km South-West (45°). After reaching their points, [P1] turns and walks to [P2]'s position. How far does [P1] walk?
templates.explanation: [P1] at N[D1], [P2] at E[D1]. Distance between them = √([D1]²+[D1]²) = [D1]√2

templates.pattern: A man walks [D1] km North-East, then [D2] km South-East, then [D3] km South-West, then [D4] km North-West. If [D1]=[D2]=[D3]=[D4], where does he end up?
templates.explanation: NE+SE+SW+NW with equal distances forms a rhombus. All N/S/E/W components cancel. Back at starting point.

templates.pattern: [P1] is at the centre of a circular park. He walks [D1] m North, [D1] m East, [D1] m South, [D1] m West, [D1] m North, [D1] m East. What is his final displacement from centre?
templates.explanation: N[D1]+E[D1]+S[D1]+W[D1] cancel each other. Then N[D1]+E[D1] remain. Net = √([D1]²+[D1]²) = [D1]√2 in NE direction.

templates.pattern: Town X is [D1] km North of town Y. Town Z is [D2] km East of Y. Town W is [D3] km South of Z. Town V is [D4] km West of W. What is the direction of V from X?
templates.explanation: Y at origin. X at N[D1]. Z at E[D2]. W at E[D2]+S[D3]. V at E[D2-D4]+S[D3]. V relative to X: E[D2-D4] and S[D1+D3]. Direction from X to V is South-East.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks from A: [D1] km East, [D2] km North, [D3] km East, [D4] km South, [D5] km West. What is the shortest distance from the final point back to A?
templates.explanation: Net E=[D1+D3-D5], Net N=[D2-D4]. Distance=√(Net_E²+Net_N²)

templates.pattern: [P1] is facing North-East. [P2] is facing the direction which is 135° clockwise from [P1]'s direction. [P3] faces the direction that is 90° anticlockwise from [P2]. What direction does [P3] face?
templates.explanation: [P1] = NE. [P2] = NE + 135° CW = SW+45° = South. [P3] = South - 90° (ACW) = East.

templates.pattern: Five friends stand in a row facing North. [P1] is to the left of [P2]. [P3] is to the right of [P2]. [P4] is between [P1] and [P2]. [P5] is to the right of [P3]. What is the order from left to right?
templates.explanation: [P1] left of [P2]. [P4] between [P1] and [P2]. [P3] right of [P2]. [P5] right of [P3]. Order: P1-P4-P2-P3-P5.

templates.pattern: [P1] starts at O facing East. Walks [D1] km, turns left, walks [D2] km, turns left, walks [D3] km, turns left, walks [D4] km, turns left, walks [D5] km. What is the final direction [P1] faces?
templates.explanation: Start East. 4 left turns = back to East (4×90°=360°). After 4 turns facing East. Then walks [D5] km East. Still facing East.

templates.pattern: [P1] walks from home: [D1] km West to A, [D2] km North to B, [D3] km East to C, [D2] km South to D, [D4] km East to E. How far is E from home and in which direction?
templates.explanation: W[D1]+N[D2]+E[D3]+S[D2]+E[D4]. N-S cancel. Net E=[D3+D4-D1]. East of home.

templates.pattern: [P1] and [P2] start from O. [P1] goes [D1] km North and [D2] km East. [P2] goes [D3] km West and [D4] km North. [P3] is at the midpoint of [P1] and [P2]. What is [P3]'s distance from O?
templates.explanation: [P1]=(E[D2],N[D1]). [P2]=(W[D3],N[D4])=(-[D3],[D4]). Midpoint [P3]=(([D2-D3])/2,([D1+D4])/2). Distance=√(midpoint components²)

templates.pattern: A ship sails [D1] km North, then [D2] km East, then [D3] km South-East (45°). What is the total Eastward displacement from start? (SE East component = [D3]/√2)
templates.explanation: Eastward = [D2] + SE_East = [D2] + [D3]/√2

templates.pattern: [P1] is at the origin. Walks to point A([D1] km East). Walks to B([D2] km North of A). Walks to C([D1] km West of B). Walks to D([D2] km South of C, which brings [P1] back to O). [P2] starts at O and walks directly to B. In what direction does [P2] walk?
templates.explanation: B is at E[D1]+N[D2] from O. Direction from O to B is North-East.

templates.pattern: A train goes [D1] km East, [D2] km North-East (45°), [D3] km North. What is the total displacement from start? (NE components: N=[D2]/√2, E=[D2]/√2)
templates.explanation: Net E=[D1]+[D2]/√2. Net N=[D3]+[D2]/√2. Displacement=√(Net_E²+Net_N²)

templates.pattern: [P1] starts from O. Goes [D1] km in direction 30° East of North (N30°E). What are the approximate North and East components? (sin30°=0.5, cos30°=0.87)
templates.explanation: N30°E means 30° from North towards East. North component=[D1]×cos30°=[D1]×0.87. East component=[D1]×sin30°=[D1]×0.5.

templates.pattern: [P1] is standing at junction J. Going [D1] km North leads to school S. Going [D2] km East from S leads to hospital H. Going [D3] km South from H leads to market M. [P2] goes directly from J to M. In which direction does [P2] go and how far?
templates.explanation: M is at E[D2]+S[D3-D1] from J (since D3>D1). Direction = South-East. Distance=√([D2]²+([D3-D1])²)

templates.pattern: [P1] walks in a pattern: 1 km East, 2 km North, 3 km West, 4 km South, 5 km East, 6 km North, 7 km West, 8 km South. What is [P1]'s displacement from start?
templates.explanation: Net E: 1-3+5-7=-4 (West). Net N: 2-4+6-8=-4 (South). Displacement = √(16+16)=4√2 km in South-West direction.

templates.pattern: [P1] goes [D1] km North from O. [P2] goes [D1] km East from O. [P3] is exactly midway between [P1] and [P2]. What is [P3]'s distance from O?

A UPSC candidate travels from home: [D1] km East to bus stop, [D2] km North to railway station, [D3] km West to exam centre, [D4] km North to college (after exam). At the end, how far is the college from home and in which direction?
templates.explanation: Net W=[D3-D1]. Net N=[D2+D4]. Direction=North-West. Distance=√(([D3-D1])²+([D2+D4])²)

templates.pattern: [P1] walks [D1] km South, [D2] km West, [D3] km North, [D4] km East, [D5] km South, [D6] km West. What is the final displacement and direction from start?
templates.explanation: Net S=[D1+D5-D3]. Net W=[D2+D6-D4]. Direction=South-West. Distance=√(Net_S²+Net_W²)
